comment: The recorded CloudWatch responses the parity fixture walks. Each group's pages are returned in order,
and the last page of a group carries no next_token. Timestamps are epoch milliseconds, as the API
returns them.
WHAT EACH ENTRY IS HERE FOR, since a fixture whose rows are undocumented decays into noise:
- The first two events of stream abc123 differ in exactly two tokens, so the second BROADENS the
first's pattern and moves its template id, its alias and its SymbolName.
- Those two arrive OUT OF TIMESTAMP ORDER, so first_seen is the minimum rather than the first arrival.
- Their severities differ, so the template's aggregate severity is the maximum over the cluster
rather than the first entry's.
- Group /aws/lambda/my_function derives the service label my_function, whose UNDERSCORE survives
into the alias; a sanitizer written as the obvious rule renders it with a dash instead.
- The event with no log_stream name exercises the alias chain's missing-first-component branch.
- The 75-character stream name exercises the 60-character truncation, which is part of the
stream's IDENTITY because the label is hashed into the stream id.
- The 12:11:30 event sits in a different epoch-aligned 5-minute window from every other event, so
it lands in its own chunk.
- The severity-prefixed and plain-text entries exercise two of the four message shapes; the JSON
bodies exercise the third.
THE DECLARED FOREIGN-GRAPH BLOCK, in the shape the client fills from the graphs this
collector's configuration entry names. It is what the production route resolves against: the
resolver matches a stream's service label against a resource's symbol_name, case-insensitively,
and ranks it by the resource_type METADATA key. The two resources in the block are exactly the
two the `resolutions` array records as expected, so a walk driven with this block produces that
array rather than being handed it.
THE BLOCK IS KEYED BY GRAPH FAMILY, and it carries no comment of its own for that reason:
every key inside cloud_context IS a family name now, so a `comment` key would decode as a
declared family whose graphs are strings. It used to be a struct with a named `cloud` field,
which ignored any key it did not know; the map form is strict, which is why this note lives
out here.
THE FAMILY IS `aws`, a name an operator registers, because there is no built-in cloud family
any more. The resolver takes EVERY declared family but code, so this name is one legitimate
value of that set and never one the production path checks for.

events.comment: The CROSS-SERVICE ERROR that makes a correlation possible. It sits in a different log group from the lambda errors, so its owning service differs, and within the detector's window of them. Without a second service no pair can correlate at all, whatever the cloud block declares.
events.message: ERROR upstream call failed after retries
plain text with no level marker

edges.comment: The declared dependency between the two resources. It is what upgrades a temporal coincidence between the two services' error templates into a CORRELATES_WITH edge; with the nodes declared and this edge absent, the pair is detected and stays unconfirmed.

resolutions.comment: The service label of the ECS group resolves to an ECS service in account acct-1.
The Lambda group's service label resolves to a function in the SAME account, so two resolutions produce two EMITTED_BY edges and two distinct proxies.
